summary: System-wide dictation for your Mac: hold a key to record, release to transcribe locally with whisper.cpp, run the text through a quick LLM cleanup, and insert it at the cursor in whatever app has focus. A floating pill shows it is live. Works offline with the local model; no accounts, no telemetry.

stack.why: global hotkeys and synthetic text insertion are native APIs
microphone capture with explicit resampling to what whisper needs
latency matters more than the last word of accuracy for dictation

stack.choice: An LLM API behind an interface, optional
stack.why: filler words and punctuation, with the raw transcript as fallback
far more reliable across apps than typing characters via CGEvent

prerequisites.name: A Mac with Apple Silicon on macOS 14 or newer
prerequisites.why: Local transcription latency is only acceptable on Apple Silicon.

prerequisites.name: Xcode 16 or newer
prerequisites.get: Mac App Store; open once to install components.

prerequisites.name: whisper.cpp built, with the small.en model
prerequisites.why: Dictation is judged on the wait. small.en answers a short clip in well under three seconds; medium roughly doubles it.
prerequisites.get: git clone https://github.com/ggml-org/whisper.cpp && cd whisper.cpp && cmake -B build && cmake --build build --config Release && ./models/download-ggml-model.sh small.en
prerequisites.verify: ./build/bin/whisper-cli -h prints usage and models/ggml-small.en.bin exists (about 500 MB)

prerequisites.name: An LLM API key for the cleanup pass (optional)
prerequisites.why: Removes filler words and fixes punctuation. Without it the raw transcript is inserted, which is still useful.
prerequisites.get: Anthropic: console.anthropic.com > API Keys. OpenAI: platform.openai.com/api-keys. Into .env; never in source.
prerequisites.cost: pay per use; fractions of a cent per dictation

prerequisites.name: A Groq key for hosted transcription (optional)
prerequisites.why: A faster path on slower machines. Local stays the default.

prerequisites.name: Two separate permissions: Input Monitoring and Accessibility
prerequisites.why: Input Monitoring lets the app observe the global hotkey; Accessibility lets it post the synthetic paste. Confusing them costs an afternoon. Each prompt appears once per launch; if dismissed, relaunch.
prerequisites.get: System Settings > Privacy & Security > Input Monitoring, and > Accessibility. Add the built app to both when prompted.

env.name: WHISPER_BIN
env.where: Path to the binary you built.

env.name: WHISPER_MODEL
env.where: small.en for latency; medium.en if accuracy matters more.

env.name: HOTKEY
env.where: The hold-to-talk key. fn, right-option, or a key combination.

env.name: ANTHROPIC_API_KEY
env.where: Anthropic console. Empty disables the cleanup pass.

env.name: LLM_MODEL
env.where: A fast, cheap model is right for a cleanup pass.

env.name: RESTORE_CLIPBOARD
env.where: true restores your previous clipboard after inserting; false leaves the transcript on it.

phases.title: Hotkey and recording
phases.goal: Hold to record, release to stop, with a WAV whisper accepts, plus hands-free, a hard cap and Esc to cancel.

steps.do: Create the Xcode project with a CLI target and the app target
steps.detail: Prove capture in the CLI target first.

steps.do: Observe the global hotkey with a CGEvent tap
steps.detail: Requires Input Monitoring. Detect key down and key up for HOTKEY. Detect a double-tap for hands-free.

steps.do: Record the microphone with AVAudioEngine while held
steps.detail: Tap the input node; on release stop and write 16 kHz mono 16-bit PCM WAV via AVAudioConverter. Not 44.1 kHz, not float.

steps.do: Add the 5-minute auto-stop and Esc to cancel
steps.detail: Observe Esc passively so it still reaches the app being typed in.

steps.do: Verify the WAV

check: Hold-record-release produces a playable 16 kHz mono 16-bit WAV
Double-tap starts and stops a hands-free session
The 5-minute cap fires
Esc discards the recording and still works normally in the foreground app
Denying Input Monitoring produces a clear message naming the pane
traps: The permission prompt appears once per launch. If the user dismisses it, the app must be relaunched before it can ask again; detect the denied state and say so.

phases.title: Transcription
phases.goal: Under three seconds from key release to text for a short clip, local by default.

steps.do: Shell out to whisper-cli with -otxt and read the result
Add the hosted path behind TRANSCRIBE_MODE with a Groq or OpenAI key
Measure latency and log it
steps.detail: Key release to transcript, in the console, so regressions are visible.

check: A 10-second clip transcribes accurately
Local works with Wi-Fi off
Key release to transcript is under three seconds for a short clip on small.en

phases.title: Cleanup pass
phases.goal: Filler removed, punctuation fixed, and never silence when the model fails.

steps.do: Write the provider interface and a fixed prompt
steps.detail: Return only the cleaned text, no preamble. Strip a leading 'Here is' defensively.

steps.do: Fall through to the raw transcript on any failure or missing key

check: 'um so like send him the thing tomorrow' becomes a clean sentence
An LLM failure still inserts the raw transcript
No response arrives wrapped in quotes or an explanation

phases.title: Insertion
phases.goal: Text appears at the cursor in any app, with the clipboard handled the way the user chose.

steps.do: Write to the pasteboard and post Cmd-V via CGEvent
steps.detail: Requires Accessibility: check AXIsProcessTrustedWithOptions and guide the user to the pane. Per-character CGEvent typing needs key-code mapping and breaks on layouts; the paste approach is the default.

steps.do: Implement RESTORE_CLIPBOARD
steps.detail: Save the previous pasteboard contents, paste, then restore after a short delay when the flag is true.

check: Dictation inserts correctly in TextEdit, a browser address bar, Slack and a terminal
The clipboard flag behaves in both positions
With Accessibility denied the app shows an actionable message
traps: Password fields refuse synthetic input by design. Say so in the README; it is not a bug to fix.

phases.title: Feedback UI
phases.goal: You always know whether it is listening.

steps.do: Build the floating pill
steps.detail: A small always-on-top panel that never takes focus, showing recording, transcribing or cleaning, the mode, and a live level meter.

steps.do: Build the menu bar item
steps.detail: On/off, launch at login, settings, recent transcripts.

check: The pill appears within 100 ms of the hotkey
It never steals focus from the app being typed into
Three distinct states are visible

phases.title: Settings, offline, README

steps.do: Read settings from a JSON file and reload on change
Verify the full path with the network off and no LLM key
Write the README
steps.detail: Both permissions and their panes, the relaunch caveat, the password-field limitation, model sizes and latency.

check: Works with the network off
A fresh Mac goes from clone to first dictation using only the README

phases.title: Distribute it
phases.goal: Notarized, self-updating, with opt-in crash reports.

steps.do: Sign with a Developer ID and notarize
Add Sparkle with a signed appcast on your domain
Add opt-in crash reporting, off by default

check: A notarized build opens on a second Mac without a right-click workaround
An appcast update is offered to an installed copy

product.outcome: A dictation tool you could ship to others: notarized, private by default, honest about the one field type it cannot type into.

architecture.swap: Per-character CGEvent typing as an alternative strategy

operations.backup: No state beyond settings.json and recent transcripts; both under ~/Library/Application Support. Time Machine covers it.
operations.incident: A leaked API key is rotated at the provider; ship a release that clears stored keys.

releaseGate: Notarized build runs on a clean Mac

notIncluded: Their tuned auto-editing voice model and per-app tone formatting.
Polish on accents, noise and crosstalk where hosted models lead.
after: Custom vocabulary passed to the cleanup prompt
Per-app cleanup styles (terse in a terminal, prose in mail)
